title: Invocation metadata reordering causes structured output mismatch under proxy retry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers are observing structured output validation failures (missing or reordered fields) when invoking external functions through the hosted API behind the proxy, particularly after transient upstream timeouts trigger the platform retry path. The issue is reproducible on Hosted and Dedicated with Private proxy enabled. Affected customers report downstream integrations failing schema validation and automated processing pipelines dropping payloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a tool/function call with multiple metadata headers and a small payload that triggers fast streaming responses
2) Introduce a transient upstream timeout at the proxy layer (simulate 50-150ms connection reset) to force a retry path
3) Observe the streamed chunks and final structured JSON output returned to the client
4) Validate the output against the expected canonical schema and note missing or reordered metadata fields in ~1-3% of requests under load
observed_behavior: When proxy retry occurs, invocation metadata entries (request_id, tool_metadata, invocation_order_tag) sometimes arrive interleaved with function output chunks rather than preserved in the canonical metadata envelope.
Parser that expects metadata envelope position fails to bind values, producing nulls or mis-ordered fields in final structured JSON.
Occurs more frequently under 95th+ percentile request latencies and with Nagle-like batching enabled on proxy connections.
expected_behavior: Metadata envelope should be preserved and emitted prior to or separate from streaming function payload chunks regardless of retry/backoff behavior.
Structured output parsers should receive canonical JSON with consistent field ordering or explicit keys so downstream schema validation never depends on arrival order.
impact_summary: 3 enterprise customers reported pipeline failures in the last 48 hours, causing delayed batch jobs and manual intervention.
Estimated token-level retries increased request cost by ~7% for affected tenants during incident window.
High priority because it leads to data loss at customer downstream processors (high trust workloads).
initial_triage_and_root_cause: Triage indicates the proxy retry path reuses a shared streaming buffer and merges buffered metadata frames with subsequent function payload frames without preserving frame boundaries.

Root cause: optimization in proxy connection pooling that attempted to collapse small metadata frames into the next payload frame to reduce RTTs. Under retry, the buffered fragment is concatenated out-of-order due to re-queue timing on the event loop.
Secondary contributor: some parsers relied on arrival ordering rather than strict field names; this made the bug visible even though JSON remained syntactically valid.
mitigations: Roll forward a proxy-side mitigation to treat metadata frames as atomic and always emit metadata envelope as a separate chunk before payload when a retry or requeue occurs (hotfix patch: proxy v1.12.3).
Short-term: disable Nagle-like coalescing on proxy tunnels for the streaming codepath (config flag proxytuning.disable_coalesce=true) until rollout completes.
Notify affected customers about a deploy schedule and offer temporary request routing to Dedicated capacity with proxy bypass if needed.
proposed_fix: 1) Update proxy frame encoder to tag metadata frames with an immutable boundary flag and implement a strict re-emit behavior on retry paths.
2) Add integrity checks in runtime: sequence numbers per invocation and per-frame checks to detect out-of-order application at ingestion.
3) Add upstream adapter tests simulating retry and requeue with interleaved small frames to ensure ordering guarantees are preserved.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): Deploy proxy v1.12.3 with atomic metadata frames to 5% of Hosted traffic in us-west-2. Monitor 95th/99th parser validation errors and token cost metrics for 48 hours.

Phase B: If canary stable, enable change for all Hosted and schedule Dedicated cluster upgrades during maintenance windows. Private customers will receive patch notes and a package for air-gapped installs.
Rollback criteria: parser-validation error delta > 0.1% over baseline or consumer-reported regressions.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests: simulate frame boundary preservation and retry paths (new test cases added to proxy/streaming_framing_test.go).
Integration: end-to-end tool invocation tests with synthetic customers validating schema binding under induced retry scenarios.
Load tests: run 95th+ latency load with and without coalescing to verify fix reduces incidence to <0.01%.
Customer verification: invite two impacted customers to run their real pipelines against canary endpoints and sign off.

notes: Avoid parser changes that assume ordering; JSON consumers should be resilient to arrival order and depend on explicit field names. We'll add guidance to SDK docs about strict envelope semantics.
Consider adding a platform-level contract test that validates envelope boundaries for any streaming protocol change in the future.
